title: Grade 11 Chemistry — Basic Concepts of Chemistry & Structure of Atom
description: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry and Structure of Atom practice questions
subject: chemistry

questions.question: The molar mass of H₂SO₄ (sulphuric acid) is:
Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³) represents:
options: Number of atoms in 1 gram of any element
Number of particles in 1 mole of substance
questions.explanation: Avogadro's number N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ is the number of elementary entities (atoms, molecules, ions) in 1 mole of any substance.

questions.question: In the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, the ratio of moles of H₂ consumed to NH₃ produced is:
questions.explanation: From stoichiometry: 3 moles H₂ produce 2 moles NH₃. Ratio H₂:NH₃ = 3:2.

questions.question: The number of moles in 44 g of CO₂ (molar mass = 44 g/mol) is:
The percentage composition of oxygen in H₂O (molar mass = 18 g/mol) is:
In a chemical reaction, the limiting reagent is:
options: The reactant that is completely consumed and limits the product formed
questions.explanation: The limiting reagent is completely consumed first, determining the maximum amount of product that can be formed. The other reactants are present in excess.

questions.question: The empirical formula of a compound represents:
options: The actual number of atoms in one molecule
The simplest whole number ratio of atoms
The molar mass of the compound
questions.explanation: The empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms. Example: H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide) has molecular formula H₂O₂ but empirical formula HO.

questions.question: One mole of an ideal gas at STP (0°C, 1 atm) occupies a volume of:
questions.explanation: At STP (0°C and 1 atm), 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 litres (molar volume). This is a standard reference used in stoichiometric calculations.

questions.question: Bohr's model of the atom was successful in explaining the spectrum of:
questions.explanation: Bohr's model successfully explained the line spectrum of hydrogen and hydrogen-like ions (He⁺, Li²⁺ etc. — one electron species) but failed for multi-electron atoms.

questions.question: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle states that:
options: Position and momentum of a particle can be determined simultaneously with infinite precision
It is impossible to determine position and momentum of a particle simultaneously with infinite precision
questions.explanation: Δx × Δp ≥ h/(4π). The more precisely we know position, the less precisely we know momentum, and vice versa. This led to the quantum mechanical model.

questions.question: The quantum numbers for the 2p subshell are:
questions.explanation: For 2p: principal quantum number n=2, azimuthal quantum number l=1 (p subshell: l=1). For s: l=0, p: l=1, d: l=2, f: l=3.

questions.question: According to Aufbau principle, electrons are filled in orbitals in order of:
questions.explanation: Aufbau (building up) principle: electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy. Order: 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p... (n+l rule).

questions.question: The electronic configuration of Sodium (Na, atomic number 11) is:
questions.explanation: Na has 11 electrons: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s¹ = 2+2+6+1 = 11. The single electron in 3s makes Na very reactive.

questions.question: Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity states that:
options: Electrons pair up in orbitals of the same energy before filling the next subshell
Electrons occupy orbitals of the same subshell singly before pairing up
No two electrons can have all four quantum numbers the same
Electrons fill in order of increasing energy
questions.explanation: Hund's rule: orbitals of the same subshell (same energy) are filled with one electron each first, all with parallel spins, before any pairing occurs.

questions.question: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the d subshell is:
questions.explanation: The d subshell has 5 orbitals (l=2, m = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2). Each orbital holds 2 electrons: 5 × 2 = 10 electrons maximum.
